title: Lead paint and older-surface awareness (refer)
audience: Painters and painting workers who work on older buildings
learningOutcomes: Recognise the signs that an older surface may contain lead paint.
Stop disturbing older surfaces until their composition is assessed by a competent specialist.
Describe the licence and regulatory position for lead paint work, which the matrix does not record.

instruction.heading: Why an older surface is a reason to stop
instruction.body: Paint on older buildings may contain lead, and the age of a building is a reason to assess the paint, not proof either way. A painted surface can have lead in the paint film even when it looks clean, and the only reliable way to know is to have it assessed. Lead is harmful when it is breathed in or swallowed, and the most common route on a painting job is dust. The job that causes the most exposure is usually the one that makes the most dust: dry sanding, scraping, grinding, abrasive blasting or heat stripping. Heat stripping can also release fumes. Children and pregnant workers face particular risk, so occupants should be kept away from the work. Because the paint cannot be judged by eye, the safe default is that an older surface is not disturbed until a competent specialist has assessed it and the result is recorded.

instruction.heading: What counts as a lead process
instruction.body: Regulators treat certain paint-removal work as a lead process. The NSW lead notification guidance lists removing paint that contains lead among the processes that involve lead (page metadata published 30 June 2021, last modified 24 September 2021). The South Australian guidance lists dry sanding, buffing and grit blasting as lead processes for removing lead paint. Victoria regulates work that sands, buffs or removes paint with lead levels greater than 1 per cent by dry weight as a lead process (WorkSafe Victoria safety alert, published 20 January 2025). The exact thresholds and duties differ between states, so a painter who is unsure whether a surface contains lead should treat it as potentially lead-bearing until the assessment says otherwise.

instruction.heading: What to do when you find an older surface
instruction.body: Where an older surface is to be disturbed, stop before any sanding, scraping, heat stripping, grinding or blasting. Keep occupants, children and other trades away from the area, and put up barrier tape. Do not dry sweep the dust, and do not use compressed air or a standard vacuum to clear it, because these spread fine dust. Record the surface, its location, its condition and the reason for the stop. Refer the surface for specialist assessment, and tell the client in writing that the painting work on that surface waits for the outcome. Do not sand a small test patch to check the paint, because the test itself releases dust. Where the assessor advises containment or cleaning methods, follow their written advice and the regulator's requirements, and do not improvise.

instruction.heading: Notification timing differs by state
instruction.body: Notice rules apply around the start of lead risk work, and the timing differs by state. In New South Wales, the notice must be given seven days before lead risk work starts (SafeWork NSW, lead notifications page). In South Australia, the person conducting the business must notify within seven days of the work being determined to be lead risk work (SafeWork SA, lead risk work page); the commencement trigger is not confirmed by an official source. In the Australian Capital Territory, the notification is due within seven days of determining that the work is lead risk work (WorkSafe ACT). In Victoria, notice to WorkSafe is required before lead-risk work begins, and the guidance gives no fixed timeframe (WorkSafe Victoria, lead-based paint removal). None of these pages names a licence for lead paint removal. Do not assume that a painting licence covers lead paint removal, and confirm the position with the state regulator before accepting any lead paint removal.

instruction.heading: Asbestos: the other older-surface question
instruction.body: Older buildings may also contain asbestos, and asbestos can look like ordinary sheeting or render. Asbestos limits differ by state. In Victoria, unlicensed removal of non-friable asbestos is limited to an area of 10 square metres in total, and to a total time of one hour of asbestos removal work in any period of seven days, which is cumulative across all employees; the page is for an employer or a self-employed person (Asbestos Victoria, unlicensed asbestos removal, which shows an 'Updated' label and no date). The Victorian page does not list friable asbestos among the unlicensed exceptions, so treat friable material as outside that allowance and confirm with the regulator. In New South Wales, less than 10 square metres of non-friable asbestos does not need a licence, and removal above that needs a class B licence, while any amount of friable asbestos needs a class A licence (Service NSW, asbestos removal licence). In Queensland, a licence is not needed for 10 square metres or less of non-friable asbestos, and any amount of friable asbestos needs a class A licence (WorkSafe Queensland). A painter who finds possible asbestos stops, keeps people clear, and refers it. Painting over asbestos-containing material is not a way round the removal rules.

instruction.heading: What this matrix does not say
instruction.body: The licence matrices used for this course record the painting licence positions but do not record a licence rule for lead paint removal. A painter should not accept lead paint removal work on the basis of a painting licence, and should confirm the state's position with the regulator before quoting, scheduling or starting. The record of that check is part of the job file.

instruction.heading: The limits of this lesson
instruction.body: Completing this lesson does not give a lead paint, asbestos or painting licence, certificate or authority to disturb older surfaces. It teaches you to recognise an older surface, to stop, to refer and to record. The assessment of lead and asbestos is done by a competent specialist.

procedure: Check the building's age and the surface's condition as a reason to assess, not as proof either way.
Do not sand, scrape, heat-strip, grind, blast or dry-sweep an older painted surface until it has been assessed.
Keep occupants, children and other trades away, and put up barrier tape around the area.
Refer the surface for specialist assessment, and record the referral, the location, the surface and the date.

Confirm the state regulator's notice timing and licence position before accepting any lead paint removal. The timing is seven days before work starts in NSW, within seven days of determination in SA (the commencement trigger is not confirmed by an official source), and within seven days of determination in the ACT, and it is before work starts in Victoria.
Record the outcome of the assessment, any written advice on containment, and the decision made.

workedExamples.situation: A client in a 1950s house asks you to sand the window frames before painting them, and says the paint looks old but has been there for years.
workedExamples.reasoning: Not before an assessment. The age of the building is a reason to assess the paint, and sanding can release lead dust. Do not sand the frames to check the paint. Refer the frames for specialist assessment, record the referral, and tell the client in writing that painting waits for the outcome. The client's view that the paint has been there for years is not an assessment.

workedExamples.situation: During a renovation you scrape a loose section of bathroom wall and find a grey sheeting with a fibrous texture behind the paint. The building is older and the owner wants the wall painted this week.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you continue scraping, and what do you tell the owner?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop scraping immediately. Fibrous sheeting may be asbestos-containing, and disturbing it can release fibres. Keep people out of the bathroom, do not dry sweep or vacuum the debris, and refer the material to a competent specialist. Tell the owner in writing that the wall cannot be painted until the material is assessed and any removal is carried out by a person who holds the required licence for the class of asbestos. Record the date, the location and the referral.

workedExamples.situation: A painter is asked to strip a set of old window frames by heat gun in a house built in an older era, with a family and a young child living there.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Heat stripping can release fumes and fine material from old paint, and occupants and a young child are at risk. Stop the request, refer the frames for assessment, and keep the household and the child away from the work area until the assessment is complete. Record the request, the refusal and the referral, and explain that any stripping method waits for the assessment outcome.

equipmentAndPpe: Barrier tape, signs and cones to keep people away from the area
Respiratory protection only where the task is authorised, the worker is trained and fit-tested, and the assessor requires it
Disposable coveralls and gloves where the assessor advises them
Heavy-duty sealable bags for debris, only where the assessor or the site advises them
Referral and record form showing location, surface, date and outcome
Phone or radio to reach the supervisor and the assessor

commonErrors.error: Sanding older paint to check whether it is lead.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not disturb the surface. Refer it for assessment.

commonErrors.error: Dry-sweeping paint dust or clearing it with compressed air.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep dust contained, do not dry sweep or blow it, and follow the assessor's written advice.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a painting licence covers lead paint removal.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the lead paint position with the state regulator before accepting the work.

commonErrors.error: Treating a small patch as too small to matter.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop for any older surface, and refer it. Size does not show whether the paint or material is hazardous.

commonErrors.error: Counting asbestos allowances per room or per job.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state's allowance, which in Victoria is 10 square metres in total and one hour in any period of seven days, cumulative across all employees, and refer anything above it.

commonErrors.error: Painting over fibrous sheeting or unknown material to avoid disturbing it.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, keep people clear, and refer. Painting does not make the material safe.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Lead notification timing (checked 2026-11-03): NSW requires notice seven days before lead risk work starts. South Australia requires notice within seven days of its determination as lead risk work; the commencement trigger is not confirmed by an official source. The ACT requires notice within seven days of determining that the work is lead risk work. Victoria requires notice before lead-risk work starts, with no fixed timeframe, and regulates work with more than 1 per cent lead by dry weight as a lead process.

Lead paint removal licence: none of the SA, NSW, Victorian or ACT pages checked names a licence for lead paint removal. The South Australian position is notification within seven days, not a licence. Any state licence requirement not named on these pages is not confirmed by an official source.

Asbestos: Victoria allows unlicensed removal of non-friable asbestos where the area to be removed does not exceed 10 square metres in total, and the total time of removal work does not exceed one hour in any period of seven days, which is cumulative across all employees, for an employer or a self-employed person. New South Wales does not require a licence for less than 10 square metres of non-friable material, requires a class B licence above that, and requires a class A licence for friable material in any amount. Queensland does not require a licence for 10 square metres or less of non-friable asbestos, and requires a class A licence for friable asbestos in any amount, with direct supervision by a nominated supervisor.
Completing this lesson does not give a lead paint, asbestos or painting licence, certificate or authority to disturb older surfaces.

qualityStandard: Older surfaces are not disturbed until a competent specialist has assessed them.
Each referral is recorded with the surface, the location, the date and the outcome.
The regulatory position, including the notice timing and any licence requirement, is confirmed with the state regulator before any removal is accepted.
documentationEvidence: Referral record for each older surface, with location, surface, date and the person referred to.
Specialist assessment outcome, with the written advice on containment and disposal.
Record of the state regulatory position check, with the state, the date, the page or the person consulted, and the result.
Asbestos allowance log, where a licence exemption is claimed, showing the area and time of each task and the running total for the period.
summary: The age of a building is a reason to assess older paint, not to disturb it.
Do not sand, scrape, heat-strip or dry-sweep an older surface until it has been assessed, and keep people away.
Confirm both before accepting the work.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks you to sand the window frames of a 1950s house to check the paint. What is correct?
options: Sand them with a mask on, since the mask keeps the dust out of the lungs
Heat-strip them quickly, since heat lifts the paint faster than sanding
Sand them wet to reduce dust, since the water keeps the paint down well
Do not sand; refer the frames for specialist assessment before disturbing them

knowledgeChecks.question: In Victoria, what level of lead in paint is regulated as a lead process when sanded or removed?
options: Greater than 1 per cent lead by dry weight
Any trace of lead at all
Greater than 10 per cent lead by wet weight

knowledgeChecks.question: In New South Wales, when must notice of lead risk work be given?
options: Notice is not needed in New South Wales
Seven days before lead risk work starts
One year after the work is finished
